items.title: Long-end yields at multi-decade highs
items.detail: The 10-year touched 5.225% on Sep 24, its highest since 2007, and the 30-year 5.502%, highest since 2004; the 5-year crossed 5% on Sep 23 for the first time since 2007. The 10-year closed the week at 5.17%. Every long-duration multiple in the book is priced against a 5% risk-free rate.

items.title: The Fed hiked and says it is not done
items.detail: A unanimous 25bp hike on Sep 16 took funds to 3.75-4.00%; 16 of 18 officials project another hike this year and BofA puts Oct 28 odds near 75%. August PCE and the Oct 2 payrolls report (consensus ~85k vs 162k) land this week — a hot print pushes yields back through 5.2%.

items.title: Oil is a binary on US-Iran talks
items.detail: Brent settled $104.32 (-2.14%) and WTI $92.41 (-2.33%) on Friday after Iran offered, with conditions, to reopen Hormuz within seven days; Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia limit the downside. A deal hits the book's four energy names; a collapse re-ignites headline inflation.

items.title: Leadership is narrow and AI-concentrated
items.detail: Tech +3.1% and healthcare +1.57% carried the week while the Russell 2000 fell 0.8% and only nine S&P names made new highs on Friday. AMD at $1T, META +16% and ALAB +25% in two weeks mean one disappointing AI data point can reverse a lot at once.

items.title: Micron's Sep 30 print is a semis-wide event
items.detail: Consensus expects ~$51bn revenue (+353%) and ~$31.52 EPS; the stock rebounded ~17% into the print. Analysts flag a gross-margin guide below ~86% as the bear trigger — a miss would hit MU, SKHY, NVDA and AMD together.

items.title: AI-infrastructure financing strain
items.detail: Oracle sent a force-majeure notice on its Project Jupiter data-centre campus (-3.4% on Sep 24) after negative FCF of $23.7bn last fiscal year; neoclouds CRWV, NBIS, IREN and APLD fell 2.5-4.4% on Friday even as Dell rose. Debt-funded buyers are being separated from hardware sellers.

items.title: Complacent volatility pricing
items.detail: VIX closed ~14.81 and high-yield spreads sit near 2.8% while the 10-year is at a 17-year high and one-year inflation expectations (UMich) rose to 4.6%. Cheap protection is a reason to hedge, not a reason to relax.
